models.name: Auto (Efficiency)
models.headline_benchmarks: No fixed benchmarks — Cursor routes to a balanced model per request
models.pricing_notes: Cursor-managed routing across the Auto + Composer pool; not a fixed model
models.best_for: Simple, well-defined, bounded tasks — routine edits, boilerplate generation, direct questions, and standard refactors where any competent model suffices and manual model selection adds no value

models.name: Claude 4.5 Haiku
models.headline_benchmarks: AA Intelligence Index 37.1; Output Speed 138.4 tokens/s; AA-Omniscience -4.2; latency leader among Claude family
models.pricing_notes: Hidden by default; Bedrock/Vertex: regional endpoints +10% surcharge; Cache: writes 1.25x, reads 0.1x
models.best_for: Speed-optimized lowest-cost Claude model, ideal for simple completions, high-volume repetitive tasks, and latency-sensitive workflows where a lightweight capable response matters more than deep reasoning

models.name: Composer 2 (Fast)
models.headline_benchmarks: CursorBench 61.3 (+37% over Composer 1.5); SWE-bench Multilingual 73.7; Terminal-Bench 2.0 61.7
models.best_for: Cursor's enforced default Composer model — purpose-built for multi-file agentic editing, fine-tuned on real developer sessions, self-summarizing 200K context for sustained long tasks, and frontier-level coding quality with speed-optimized inference at the lowest output price ($2.50/M) — the default choice for standard implementation, multi-file changes, and roadmap execution where coding-A is sufficient

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Pro
models.headline_benchmarks: AA Intelligence Index 57.2 (#3); AA-Omniscience 32.9 (#1); HLE 44.7% (#1); LMArena Text Elo 1483.6 (#4); 1M-token context
models.best_for: True native multimodal understanding (text, image, video, audio, and code in a single pass), 1M-token context optimized for heterogeneous inputs, strong agentic multi-step tool use, and synthesizing insights across large mixed-media datasets or sprawling document corpora — the obvious choice whenever multimodal or long-context is the primary category

models.name: GPT-5.2
models.headline_benchmarks: MMLU Pro 81.4; GPQA 71.2; LiveCodeBench 66.9; 400K-token context; output speed 68 tokens/s; released 2025-12-10
models.pricing_notes: Hidden by default; Agentic and reasoning capabilities; Available reasoning effort variant is gpt-5.2-high
models.best_for: Earlier-flagship GPT reasoning model (December 2025) with 400K context and broad knowledge coverage (GPQA 71.2, MMLU Pro 81.4); same medium-tier pricing as GPT-5.3 Codex but lacks Codex's autonomous-coding specialization — pick gpt-5.3-codex over gpt-5.2 for coding/agentic tasks; gpt-5.2 fits when broad reasoning at A-tier knowledge and a 400K context window are the primary need at the medium price tier

models.name: GPT-5.3 Codex
models.headline_benchmarks: GPT-5.3 Codex (xhigh) listed on AA leaderboards; Codex lineage retains strong Terminal-Bench and SWE-bench Verified performance for autonomous coding
models.pricing_notes: Requires Max Mode on request-based plans; Agentic and reasoning capabilities; Available reasoning effort variant is gpt-5.3-codex-high
models.best_for: Highest terminal and tool-use proficiency at the medium tier, most token-efficient autonomous coding, excels at long-running agentic sessions spanning debugging through deployment, and hard algorithmic problems requiring sustained code reasoning across languages — the cost-efficient pick for pure coding and agentic execution when an S-tier coding rating is needed

models.name: GPT-5.4
models.headline_benchmarks: AA Intelligence Index 56.8 (#4); LMArena Text Elo 1454.1 (#18); GPT-5.4 (xhigh) Output Speed 83.2 tokens/s; lowest factual error rate among GPT models
models.pricing_notes: Hidden by default; Requires Max Mode on request-based plans; Agentic and reasoning capabilities; 90% discount on cached input tokens; Fast mode is 15% faster with 2x pricing; Long context (Max Mode) supports up to 1M tokens with 2x input pricing
models.best_for: Broadest professional domain expertise (outperforms human specialists in 83% of occupations), native computer-use capability surpassing human baselines, lowest factual error rate among GPT models, and cross-domain knowledge work requiring deep real-world accuracy and grounding

models.name: GPT-5.4 Mini
models.headline_benchmarks: AA Intelligence Index 48.9 (xhigh); Output Speed 171.4 tokens/s; HLE 19.4% (GPT-5-mini)
models.pricing_notes: Hidden by default; Smaller, faster variant of GPT-5.4; 90% discount on cached input tokens
models.best_for: Lightweight GPT-5.4 variant balancing quality and cost, well-suited for straightforward coding, short-form generation, and high-throughput workloads needing solid GPT reasoning at a fraction of the flagship price

models.name: GPT-5.4 Nano
models.headline_benchmarks: Cheapest GPT-5 family variant; throughput-optimized inference
models.pricing_notes: Hidden by default; Smallest GPT-5.4 variant, optimized for cost; 90% discount on cached input tokens
models.best_for: Ultra-low-cost GPT variant for trivial text tasks, simple lookups, rapid classification, and extreme-throughput pipelines where cost efficiency is the sole constraint and task complexity is minimal

models.name: GPT-5.5
models.headline_benchmarks: AA Intelligence Index 60.2 (#1); LMArena Text Elo 1462.5 (#14); HLE 44.3%; AA-Omniscience 20.1 (#3)
models.pricing_notes: Requires Max Mode on request-based plans; Agentic and reasoning capabilities; More token-efficient than GPT-5.4 on comparable tasks; Improved persistence on long-running tasks; Fast mode is available at higher rates; Long context (Max Mode) supports up to 1M tokens with 2x input pricing
models.best_for: OpenAI's most capable frontier model and highest-cost GPT offering, best suited for the most demanding reasoning, long-horizon planning, and tasks where maximum intelligence is required regardless of cost — strongest single model for hard coding, agentic execution, and reasoning, but verify factual claims due to elevated hallucination

models.name: Grok 4.3
models.headline_benchmarks: AA Intelligence Index 53.2 (#7); AA-Omniscience 18.3 (#4); HLE 35.0%; LMArena Search Elo 1199
models.pricing_notes: Requires Max Mode on request-based plans
models.best_for: Latest Grok release with built-in multi-agent self-verification, configurable reasoning depth, and signature 2M-token context with hallucination-resistant grounding — leads the low tier on agentic execution and long-context, ideal when massive context, factual accuracy, and aggressive cost efficiency must coexist

models.name: Opus 4.7
models.headline_benchmarks: AA Intelligence Index 57.3 (#2); LMArena Text #6 (Elo 1478.7); LMArena WebDev #2 (Elo 1559.3); AA-Omniscience 26.2 (#2)
models.pricing_notes: Requires Max Mode on request-based plans; Up to 1M tokens in Max Mode at the same per-token rates (no long-context surcharge)
models.best_for: Deepest abstract and scientific reasoning, highest coherence on long unsupervised multi-step agent chains, best long-context recall at 1M tokens, 128K output ceiling for large single-shot deliverables, and novel problem-solving where high ambiguity demands creative judgment over pattern-matching

models.name: Premium (Intelligence)
models.pricing_notes: Cursor-managed routing mode; bills at the routed model's API rate; carries that model's pricing-notes for the duration of the request
models.best_for: Cursor auto-selects the strongest available model; best when the task is clearly high-complexity but does not map to one specific model's niche advantage, or when you are uncertain which frontier model's strengths best apply

models.name: Sonnet 4.6
models.headline_benchmarks: AA Intelligence Index 51.7; LMArena WebDev Elo 1523.6 (#6); AA-Omniscience 12.4; top-ranked tool-calling on Anthropic lineage
models.pricing_notes: Requires Max Mode on request-based plans; Up to 1M tokens in Max Mode at the same per-token rates (no long-context surcharge)
models.best_for: Top-ranked tool-calling and agentic execution globally, near-Opus coding quality at 2-3x the speed, strong mathematical reasoning (89% MATH), and complex but well-structured tasks needing reliable high-throughput multi-step implementation

access_methods.name: Anthropic API
access_methods.best_for: Programmatic / scripted Claude use outside Claude Code — raw API headers, batch endpoints, or features not surfaced by Claude Code. Falls back here when claude.ai Max budget is exhausted.

access_methods.name: ChatGPT (web / desktop)
access_methods.best_for: Chat-driven GPT use without terminal or IDE integration; subscription-funded so marginal cost is $0 until ChatGPT's usage limits kick in.

access_methods.name: Claude Code
access_methods.best_for: Default for Claude coding or terminal tasks when a claude.ai Max subscription is active — $0 marginal cost until the Max budget is exhausted, full tool-use surface, runs as a CLI and as an IDE extension inside Cursor. Heavy Opus usage that would cost over $1,000/mo on per-token API is fully covered by a $100/mo Max plan.

access_methods.name: claude.ai web / desktop
access_methods.best_for: Chat-driven Claude use (no terminal, no codebase tool use) under the same Max budget that funds Claude Code — pick when the task is conversational rather than code-editing.

access_methods.name: Codex
access_methods.best_for: Default for GPT-driven autonomous coding sessions when a ChatGPT Plus/Pro subscription is active — pays from the ChatGPT budget instead of the per-token API rate. Best surface for gpt-5.3-codex on long-running terminal / agentic work.

access_methods.name: Cursor
access_methods.best_for: Cursor IDE — single Platform covering both UI modes (Composer for multi-file autonomous editing; Chat for interactive model-picker). The operator picks the mode at task time based on the chosen Model: composer-2 / auto / premium imply Composer mode; frontier models (opus-4.7, gpt-5.5, sonnet-4.6, etc.) imply Chat mode. All routes through the $0-marginal Cursor pool. Defer to claude-code when the chosen model is Claude and claude.ai Max is active (Max budget is cheaper marginal cost than burning Cursor pool tokens on Claude calls that have a dedicated Anthropic subscription path).

access_methods.name: Gemini (web / app)
access_methods.best_for: Chat-driven Gemini use under the Gemini Advanced subscription budget.

access_methods.name: Gemini CLI
access_methods.best_for: Terminal-driven Gemini use; the CLI surface for multimodal and long-context Gemini work outside Cursor's pool.

access_methods.name: Google AI Studio API
access_methods.best_for: Programmatic / scripted Gemini use with a Google API key. Pay-per-token at Google's published rates.

access_methods.name: OpenAI API
access_methods.best_for: Programmatic / scripted GPT use when an OpenAI API key is configured. Pay-per-token at OpenAI's published rates.

access_methods.name: xAI API
access_methods.best_for: Direct Grok API access for 2M-context or hallucination-resistant tasks; pay-per-token at xAI's published rates.

cursor_2x_input.rule: Long context (Max Mode) supports up to 1M tokens with 2x input pricing
